clue.text: Plot to beat chaotic situation

parts.note: a plot of garden ground is a bed
to lam is to thrash or beat

explanation.surface: Someone plots to defeat a state of chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, after the old London asylum, is any scene of uproar and confusion.

clue.text: Muscle got from second-grade mushrooms I consumed

parts.note: B is the second grade after A
ceps are edible boletus mushrooms

explanation.surface: A muscle is built from eating inferior mushrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is the large muscle at the front of the upper arm.

clue.text: Ring dishing dirt about someone ultimately

definitions.text: Ring dishing dirt about someone ultimately

parts.note: a disc is a ring-shaped flat object

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, surrounding, the final letter
dishing means messing up or ruining, so the letters are jumbled
ultimately points to the last letter of someone

explanation.surface: A gang spreading scandal about someone in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishing' rearranges DIRT and 'about' wraps it round E. The whole clue describes a smear campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit someone is to damage their reputation, as a ring spreading gossip does.

clue.text: Programmes finish in a fun occasion

indicators.note: the finish goes in the fun occasion

parts.note: a gas is informal for an enjoyable time
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Television programmes end at a jolly event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Programmes' looks like broadcasts but means plans for meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: Agendas are lists of items to be dealt with, plans of business.

clue.text: Two muscles I have in case

parts.note: abs (abdominal muscles) gives AB and lats (latissimus dorsi) gives LAT
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having two muscles in a carrying case.
explanation.definitionFit: The ablative is a grammatical case in Latin, marking means or separation.

clue.text: Accountant needs to stand article on bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above

parts.note: to be is to stand or exist
an is the indefinite article
a counter is a bar where goods or drinks are served

explanation.surface: An accountant must stand up a newspaper piece on a pub bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean counter is a disparaging nickname for an accountant or bureaucrat obsessed with figures.

clue.text: Some spread harm and unrighteousness

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people spread harm and wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu thought adharma is unrighteousness, the opposite of dharma or moral law.

clue.text: Going round circuit, length one mile, a racetrack

indicators.note: the other letters go round, surrounding, the circuit

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a circuit is a ring, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A driver laps a mile-long circuit at a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Imola in northern Italy hosts a motor-racing circuit used for Grand Prix events.

clue.text: Creature roaming the planet endlessly

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so the letters wander into a new order
endlessly means the last letter of planet is dropped

explanation.surface: A beast roams the Earth for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts PLANET to PLANE; 'roaming' rearranges THE PLANE.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant is a large animal, a typical example of a creature.

clue.text: Company's determined to indulge

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, plus the 'S
set means determined, as in set on winning

explanation.surface: A firm is resolved to pamper someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper or spoil someone.

clue.text: Garment engineering graduate gets about a pound

indicators.note: the graduate's letters get round the rest, enclosing them

parts.note: BE is a Bachelor of Engineering
to throb is to pound or pulsate

explanation.surface: A newly qualified engineer buys a dressing gown for about a pound sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money but is the verb to throb.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathrobe is a loose robe worn before or after bathing, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Standard I set in a record of Nirvana

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

indicators.note: I is set in, placed inside, the record

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

explanation.surface: A standard set by a record by the band Nirvana.
explanation.walkthrough: Nirvana looks like the rock band; here it is the state of bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradisic means belonging to paradise, a heavenly bliss like nirvana.

clue.text: Feature of election night gets more excited covering victory

indicators.note: the agitated letters cover, enclosing, the victory
excited means agitated, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: a win is a victory

explanation.surface: Election night grows more thrilling as a victory comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' gives SGOMETER from GETS MORE; 'covering' puts WIN inside. The swingometer is the BBC's election-night graphic showing vote swing.
explanation.definitionFit: The swingometer, a dial showing party vote shifts, is a staple of British election coverage.

clue.text: Little auk catches a fish

indicators.note: the bird's name catches, holding inside it, the letter a

parts.note: roch or rotch is a dialect name for the little auk, a small seabird

explanation.surface: A small seabird catches a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a silvery freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Upper-class girl set about in spreading hypocrisy

indicators.note: the turned letters go in the spreading

parts.note: dilation is a spreading or widening

indicators.note: set about means turned round, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A posh girl gets stuck into spreading hypocrisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' turns the upper-class girl round, giving SSIMU; 'in' then puts that inside the word for spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissimulation is concealing one's true feelings, a form of hypocritical pretence.

clue.text: Cross brief entering popular court

indicators.note: the brief word enters the popular and the court

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
terse means brief

explanation.surface: An angry, curt lawyer enters a well-liked court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry but is the verb to cross.
explanation.definitionFit: To intersect is to cut across or cross one another.

clue.text: Comprehensive school's initial greeting

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of school's

parts.note: in Scots, to greet means to weep

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school's welcome to new pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' looks like a British state school; it is the adjective. 'greeting' is the Scots verb to greet, cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping means wide-ranging, as in sweeping changes, i.e. all-embracing.

clue.text: Letting waters flow the old way

indicators.note: letting the letters flow freely rearranges them

explanation.surface: Releasing water the traditional way.
explanation.walkthrough: WATLING STREET is an ancient Roman road across England from Dover to Wroxeter.
explanation.definitionFit: This road was laid out in Roman times, so it is literally an old way.

clue.text: I serve a captain in religious role

parts.note: one who serves a ship's captain is a mate, so after I this reads as 'm a mate, I am a mate

explanation.surface: A sailor says he serves under a captain in a church role.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M A MATE: a ship's mate serves the captain.
explanation.definitionFit: An imamate is the office of an imam, a Muslim prayer leader.

clue.text: Leave country spurning good Arab land

indicators.note: spurning means rejecting, so the letter for good is thrown out

parts.note: to emigrate is to leave one's country

explanation.surface: Someone emigrates, rejecting a decent Arab country.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir, as in the Gulf.

clue.text: Old rifle made of bone

parts.note: to rifle is to ransack and steal

explanation.surface: An old gun with a bone stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun but is the verb to rob.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal means bony, relating to or composed of bone.

clue.text: Over yielding leg bye perhaps

definitions.meaning: in cricket a leg bye is a run not scored off the bat

explanation.surface: A cricket over yields a leg bye.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra is both surplus, over and above, and a cricket run such as a leg bye or wide.

clue.text: With listening device on phone, newspaperman made recording

parts.note: a tap is a bug attached to a phone line
ED is short for editor, a newspaperman

explanation.surface: A journalist bugs a phone and records the call.
explanation.definitionFit: Taped means recorded on tape, i.e. having made a recording.

clue.text: Festival to enjoy with artist in bar

indicators.note: the enjoying and the artist go in the bar

parts.note: a Mars bar is a British chocolate bar
to dig is slang for to enjoy
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A festival to have fun at with a painter in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is a Mars bar, a British chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras, Shrove Tuesday, is celebrated with carnival festivities.

clue.text: Introduces part of Bible in psalm I arranged

indicators.note: the testament goes in the rearranged letters
arranged means put in a new order, so psalm I is rearranged

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone sets passages from scripture into a psalm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' makes IMPLAS from PSALM I; 'in' puts NT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To implant is to introduce or insert something firmly.

clue.text: Servant attending earl's farewell

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the earl's letter follows the servant

parts.note: a valet is a manservant

explanation.surface: A manservant waiting on a nobleman bids goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Valete is Latin for goodbye, said to several people, used as a leaving speech.

clue.text: Terrible tragedy with end of leg caught in machinery

indicators.note: the leg's last letter is caught inside the anagram
terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters are wrecked and reformed
the end of the word leg is its final letter

explanation.surface: A dreadful accident where a leg was trapped in machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' turns TRAGEDY into GADETRY; 'caught in' puts G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadgetry means devices and mechanical contrivances collectively.

clue.text: The Italian with fast pulse

parts.note: Lent is the Christian fast before Easter
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian with a quick heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a heartbeat and 'fast' like speed; both mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of legumes, and the lentil is one.
